title: Fisetin as a Blueprint for Senotherapeutic Agents – Elucidating Geroprotective and Senolytic Properties with Molecular Modeling

Quercetin — a compound very similar to Fst- and its derivatives exhibit senolytic potential, including direct binding to the hydrophobic groove formed by BH3 domain of Bcl-2 and Bcl-xL proteins and halting their guarding properties against apoptosis, as evidenced by combined experimental and theoretical studies from Tzakos’ group.109-112 Given the structural homology between these compounds, the possibility that Fst interacts directly with Bcl-2 family proteins was examined.
The exceptional senotherapeutic activity of fisetin, combining both geroprotective and senolytic effects, was validated using computational chemistry tools, establishing it as a cornerstone template for the development of novel agents.

Selectivity towards inhibiting the Bcl-xL protein is a more pharmacologically reasonable and preferred mechanism of action that senolytics should exhibit. While Bcl-2 demonstrates visibly greater affinity for anionic forms, primarily due to favorable electrostatic interactions, Bcl-xL binds neutral molecules better and has a lower tolerance for highly charged compounds compared to Bcl-2.
